title: Instrumentation with OpenTelemetry
subtitle: Separate instrumentation from its destination
summary: Pip installs instrumentation and immediately sees HTTP calls, but not the promotion rule behind a failed checkout. OpenTelemetry separates recording operations from handling and exporting them. Custom domain context completes the baseline without binding every library to one backend.

concepts.title: API and SDK have different jobs
concepts.body: Pip’s shared client library creates spans through the instrumentation API. The SDK supplies the configured implementation that processes those calls and handles telemetry. Keeping the roles separate leaves application-wide export choices to the application. Pip can reuse instrumented libraries without forcing every caller to adopt one destination.

concepts.title: Export is a replaceable boundary
concepts.body: Pip changes telemetry backends without rewriting span creation. Exporters translate and send data; a collector can receive and process it outside the application. That replaceable boundary limits instrumentation changes. Pip still validates supported attributes, processing, and analysis because destinations are not interchangeable in every capability.

concepts.title: Automatic coverage establishes a baseline
concepts.body: Pip’s automatic coverage shows framework work and outbound HTTP timing. It quickly exposes service relationships without wrapping every operation manually. Generic libraries do not know why a discount was chosen. Pip evaluates coverage against real investigative questions before declaring instrumentation complete.

concepts.title: Custom context completes the picture
concepts.body: Pip records the chosen pricing rule where the order code evaluates it. Manual instrumentation adds meaningful operations and attributes beyond generic coverage. Consistent names support comparison across services and requests. Pip attaches context to the relevant span instead of inventing another vocabulary at every boundary.

misconceptions.claim: OpenTelemetry is itself the storage and analysis backend.
misconceptions.correction: It supplies instrumentation and telemetry handling; retained storage and investigation require a destination.
It observes supported library behavior; domain operations and attributes still need deliberate instrumentation.

scenario.title: Generic traces miss the business decision
scenario.context: An order fails only under one promotion, but automatic HTTP spans contain no promotion context.

options.label: Add the selected promotion to the relevant span
options.benefit: Makes the failing business cohort searchable.
options.cost: Requires understanding the decision point and maintaining the attribute.
options.consequence: Promotion-specific failures become a cohort the investigator can compare.

options.label: Enable additional generic HTTP hooks
options.cost: May still omit the application decision behind the failure.
options.consequence: Transport visibility improves without necessarily exposing the selected promotion.

scenario.debrief: Choose instrumentation based on the missing question, not only on how many spans it produces.

quiz.question: A library should emit spans without choosing every application’s backend. Which separation helps?
options: Instrumentation API separated from configured SDK and exporters
One globally configured backend exporter embedded in the reusable library
A different vendor-specific instrumentation interface in each application
quiz.explanation: The API exposes instrumentation while application-level configuration controls telemetry handling.

quiz.question: HTTP traces are complete but cannot distinguish pricing rules. What should be added?
options: Another exporter of the same fields
A pricing-rule attribute at the decision point
quiz.explanation: The missing fact is application context, not transport capacity.

quiz.question: What should a backend migration preserve and verify?
options: Equivalent event volume, without checking whether attributes survive
Identical dashboard totals, without checking request relationships
Span context, useful attributes, and successful export to the new destination
quiz.explanation: Portable instrumentation still needs end-to-end validation that the evidence remains usable.
